kural:34.reading: To be spotless in mind is the whole of virtue, and everything else is noisy show.

kural:269.reading: Even leaping past death becomes possible for those who have attained the power of austerity.

tamil: யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு அறுப்பான் வானோர்க்கு
kural:346.reading: One who cuts off the pride of saying 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods'.

kural:351.reading: A joyless birth comes from the confusion that perceives what isn't real as real.

kural:355.reading: Whatever a thing is and of whatever nature, seeing the true thing in that thing is understanding.

kural:391.reading: Learn what is to be learned without flaw, and having learned, stand in keeping with it.

kural:423.reading: Whatever is heard, from whoever's mouth, understanding is seeing the true substance of that very thing.

naladiyar:6.reading: The appointed span of days cannot be exceeded and no one here has leapt clear of Death and escaped; you who hold great wealth, give it away, for tomorrow the funeral drum may sound.

naladiyar:47.reading: The fool calls out 'broad-shouldered one, bangle-wearer' to a pot that seeps filth from nine openings and churns with slime, because its covering of dark skin dazzles his eyes.

naladiyar:136.reading: No one despises the ferryman for being of the lowest of the old castes, but crosses the river with his help; so take what is good from a man who has learned books, whatever his birth.

naladiyar:140.reading: Of all the many kinds of learning, studying worldly books while leaving the books of wisdom unread amounts only to clamour; there is no one who knows how to make confusion leave by that means.

tirumanthiram:270.reading: The ignorant say love and Siva are two; no one knows that love itself is Siva; once they know it, they rest as love that is Siva.

tirumanthiram:301.reading: Who knows the Lord of the gods, the divine form? Once you know him, recite, listen and realise; those who recited and realised stood exalted.

tirumanthiram:343.reading: Fools say the Ancient One, with water in his red matted hair, burned the three cities; the three cities are the work of the three impurities, and who knows that it was these he shot?

tirumanthiram:722.reading: If you can tie fast, so that it does not escape, the horse that rose with twelve legs, and drink deeply, the body will not leave for a thousand years of water and a thousand of earth; this is the Lord Nandi's command.

tirumanthiram:725.reading: I once held the body to be a thing of shame; then within the body I saw the true substance, and knowing that the Highest has made the body his temple, I now cherish it.

tirumanthiram:1442.reading: When the truth beyond speech is attained, the five that are hard to curb subside, knowledge shines above as the light of a lamp, and union with the Supreme becomes one's station.

tirumanthiram:1532.reading: For those who say he is within and without, our Lord is within and without; for those who say he is neither within nor without, he is neither within nor without.

tirumanthiram:1695.reading: When the Lord, for its beauty, takes his place in a mind made pure like a great jewel polished by work, deeds strong as weeds depart and one sees his anklet-bearing holy feet, and grace comes.

tirumanthiram:1697.reading: He who considers how the real and the unreal stand, melts his mind, bows when Siva's grace points the way so as to gain knowledge through devotion, and whose desire is fit for the Shakti of bliss: he is the true disciple.

tirumanthiram:1823.reading: For the generous Lord the heart is the great temple, the body of flesh the shrine and the mouth the tower gate; for those clear through and through, the soul is the Sivalinga, and the five thieving senses are the bright lamps.

tirumanthiram:1896.reading: When speech and mind are both still, that is silence; if only speech falls silent, one is merely mute; the pure are those in whom speech and mind are silent, and who knows the purity they bring about?

tirumanthiram:2017.reading: There is no difference called soul and Siva; souls do not know Siva, and once souls know Siva, souls remain as Siva.

tirumanthiram:2020.reading: To me, who did not know the nature of the thirty-six, Nandi made known the nature of the thirty-six; after I knew it by his grace, he stood beyond the thirty-six.

tirumanthiram:2166.reading: Considering how the five stubborn malas work through the five long states, one who sees all five plainly while fully awake stands always with the Supreme.

tirumanthiram:2382.reading: The six ends all go and subside in that known; the knower too subsides in the known of the six ends; when even the stated mark of knowledge departs, the clear silence becomes Siva's bliss.

tirumanthiram:2820.reading: I searched, calling it 'I' and calling it 'He', and as I searched, the First of knowledge who is the 'I' granted me that 'I' and 'He' are not two; and I, the one who said 'I', ceased to think.

tirumanthiram:2951.reading: Self destroyed, wealth destroyed, the long-lasting flesh destroyed, life destroyed with it, the sky destroyed and the mind destroyed, I do not know that I too was destroyed.

thiruppugazh:22.reading: The poet asks when, with Death turned back and the craving for women gone, the three gunas ended, day and night left behind and the senses' agitation cut, singing poems on the lotus feet and knowing Senthil and Kandan ever deeper, his mind will melt and dissolve, his speech end and his own action perish, so that he gains the vision of Murugan. The praise shows Indra crying 'refuge' and regaining his city, Devayanai gaining Murugan's arms, the demons dying, and the child Murugan toddling with bells and anklets ringing until Sankari's heart melts.

thiruppugazh:343.reading: The poet seems to rebuke himself ('fie!') for having tasted jivanmukti and experience, burning the three cities to ash and uprooting the sheath of sleep, and yet, not knowing how to stay settled in grace, having run off and let go; he asks Murugan to hold him so he does not end on the ruined road and to grant the lotus feet. The praise names Siva with trident, deer and axe and Uma at his side, whose golden guru Murugan is, and lists the shrines where Murugan receives worship three times a day: Kasi, Madurai, the seven hills, Kovalur, Vedaranyam, Kazhi, Arur, Puliyur, Kalatti, Chiramalai and Kanchi.

tamil: அனித்த மான வூனாளு மிருப்ப தாக வேநாசி
தவத்தி லேகு வால்மூலி புசித்து வாடு மாயாச
செனித்த காரி யோபாதி யொழித்து ஞான ஆசார
செகத்தி யாவும் வேறாக நிகழ்ச்சி யாம நோதீத
thiruppugazh:355.reading: The poet asks not to become a foolish yogi of desire and illusion who, thinking this impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath so it does not leave the nostrils and withers in austerity eating herbs; he asks instead that, with malam, maya and their adjuncts removed, devoted to the conduct of knowledge, knowing 'I am other, my body is other, the whole world is other', he be ruled as a yogi of Siva's own form beyond the mind. The praise names Gopala of the thousand names who plays the flute as uncle, Murugan of Vayalur, and the grove-circled Kavai watered by the Kaveri's flood, which all world-rulers revere.

thiruppugazh:581.reading: The poet says that though he is a great sinner walking maya's twisted way, with infatuation, desire and anger unceasing, Murugan is now his mother and father; he has not studied the four Vedas or the Agamas, so that his days not pass in vain he asks for the teaching of knowledge beyond the thirty-six. The praise names the child adorned with fragrant sandal, Murugan of Vayalur and Viralimalai, the six-faced son of the lord of ghouls and goblins, foe of Sura, lord of the gods.

thiruppugazh:1011.reading: The poet asks when, hearing what the rival sects call the ultimate (form, the formless, a light that is neither, space, heaven, the pillar holding the worlds) and seeing the reality itself, he will rest in awareness and silence, strive for the highest state, not be bewildered by the pleasures of touch, sight, smell and sound, and be freed from the pit of deceitful women into which he, guilty of the five great sins, has fallen. The praise shows the gods crying 'Hara Hara, Siva's son Skanda, refuge!' and Murugan saying 'fear not', the vel that tore the asura's chest, the emerald peacock, and Brahma, Vishnu and Siva praising him.

dialectics.note: Kural 351 says inglorious birth comes from taking what is not real as real (பொருளல்லவற்றைப் பொருளென்று உணரும் மருள்). 1697 makes the first mark of the true disciple that he considers how the real and the unreal stand (சத்தும் அசத்தும் எவ்வாறென), and then joins that discernment to devotion and grace. The Kural names the error; Tirumular builds the cure into the disciple's training.
dialectics.lens_en: In an age of synthetic media and fluent AI output, Kural 351 names the error of taking the unreal for the real (மருள்), and Tirumular 1697 makes weighing the real and the unreal (சத்தும் அசத்தும்) the first mark of a true disciple.
dialectics.lens_ta: செயற்கை ஊடகங்களும் சரளமான AI வெளியீடுகளும் பெருகும் காலத்தில், பொருளல்லாததைப் பொருளாக உணரும் மருளைக் குறள் 351 சுட்டுகிறது; சத்தும் அசத்தும் எவ்வாறு என்று ஆராய்வதை நல்ல சீடனின் முதல் அடையாளமாகத் திருமந்திரம் 1697 வைக்கிறது.

dialectics.note: Kural 346 says one who cuts off the pride of saying 'I' and 'mine' (யான் எனது என்னும் செருக்கு) enters a world above the gods. 2820 goes past cutting pride: after the gift that 'I' and 'He' are not two, even the 'I' that said 'I' ceases to think (நான்என்ற நானும் நினைப்பு ஒழிந்தேனே). The Kural's renunciation of the ego is carried to its disappearance in knowledge.
dialectics.lens_en: As AGI ends the human monopoly on cognition, Kural 346 treats cutting off the pride of 'I' and 'mine' as an ascent, and Tirumular 2820 carries it further: the 'I' that said 'I' falls quiet in knowledge. Neither verse counts this as a loss.
dialectics.lens_ta: மனித அறிவின் தனியுரிமை முடியும் காலத்தில், ‘யான் எனது’ என்னும் செருக்கை அறுப்பதைக் குறள் 346 உயர்வாகக் காண்கிறது; திருமந்திரம் 2820 அதை மேலும் தொடர்கிறது: ‘நான்’ என்று சொன்ன நானும் ஞானத்தில் நினைப்பு ஒழிகிறது. இரண்டுமே இதை இழப்பாகக் கருதவில்லை.

dialectics.note: Thiruppugazh 22 asks for the day when his mind loosens and dissolves, his speech ends and his own action perishes (சிந்தையும் அவிழ்ந்து அழிந்து உரையொழித்து என்செயல் அழிந்து) so that he sees Murugan. Tirumanthiram 1896 says silence is speech and mind both stilled, and that speech alone falling silent is mere muteness (வாக்கு மனமும் இரண்டும் மவுனமாம் ... மூங்கையாம்). The song asks for the end of mind as well as speech, which is the silence the Tirumanthiram counts as true.
dialectics.lens_en: Language models run on nonstop next-token output. These verses draw a line our own minds need: a silent tongue alone is only muteness (மூங்கை); true silence (மவுனம்) is speech and mind stilled together. No amount of output stands in for that.
dialectics.lens_ta: மொழி மாதிரிகள் இடைவிடாத சொல் உற்பத்தியில் இயங்குகின்றன. நம் மனத்துக்கே தேவையான ஒரு கோட்டை இந்தப் பாடல்கள் வரைகின்றன: வாய் மட்டும் மூடுவது மூங்கை; வாக்கும் மனமும் சேர்ந்து அடங்குவதே மவுனம். எவ்வளவு சொல் உற்பத்தியும் அதற்கு ஈடாகாது.

dialectics.note: 343 says fools take the burning of the three cities literally; the three cities are the work of the three impurities (முப்புரமாவது மும்மல காரியம்). Thiruppugazh 343 speaks of the seeker burning the forest of the three cities to ash and uprooting the sheath of sleep on the way to jivanmukti (முப்புரக் காடு நீறெழச் சாடி ... சீவன் முத்தியில்). Arunagiri applies Tirumular's inward reading to the seeker's own release.
dialectics.lens_en: Tirumular reads the burning of the three cities as inward: they are the work of the three impurities (மும்மலம்). Arunagiri applies that reading to his own release. The lesson travels to AI alignment: some of the bugs to patch are in the people doing the aligning.
dialectics.lens_ta: முப்புரம் எரித்ததைத் திருமூலர் அகத்தே நடப்பதாகப் படிக்கிறார்: முப்புரம் மும்மலத்தின் காரியம். அருணகிரியார் அந்த வாசிப்பைத் தம் விடுதலைக்கே பொருத்துகிறார். AI ஒத்திசைவுக்கும் இது பொருந்தும்: சரிசெய்ய வேண்டிய சில பிழைகள் ஒத்திசைப்பவர்களிடமே உள்ளன.

dialectics.note: The Thiruppugazh song lists what rival sects call the ultimate (உருவென அருவென ... ஒளியென வெளியென) and asks to see the reality itself in silence; 1532 says the Lord is within and without for those who say so, and neither for those who say neither. 1532 gives a reason why each sect's formula seems confirmed, while the song turns from all the formulas to a silent seeing.
dialectics.lens_en: Tirumular says each sect finds the Lord it describes: within and without for those who say so, neither for those who say neither. Arunagiri turns from all the formulas to a silent seeing. Every frame, a sect's creed or an AI system's objective, tends to find what it was built to find.
dialectics.lens_ta: ஒவ்வொரு சமயமும் தான் சொல்லும் இறைவனையே காண்கிறது என்கிறார் திருமூலர்: உள்ளும் புறமும் என்பவர்க்கு உள்ளும் புறமும், இரண்டுமில்லை என்பவர்க்கு இரண்டுமில்லை. அருணகிரியார் எல்லா வரையறைகளிலிருந்தும் திரும்பி மோனக் காட்சியை நாடுகிறார். ஒவ்வொரு சட்டகமும், அது சமயமானாலும் AI அமைப்பின் இலக்கானாலும், தான் காணும்படி கட்டப்பட்டதையே காண முனைகிறது.

dialectics.note: Kural 34 makes a spotless mind (மனத்துக்கண் மாசிலன் ஆதல்) the whole of virtue. 1695 takes the pure mind further: polished like a great gem by work (தொழிலார மாமணித் தூய்தான சிந்தை), it is where the Lord takes his place, and then deeds fall away and his feet are seen. The Kural's end becomes Tirumular's precondition for grace.
dialectics.lens_en: AI governance often stops at external compliance rules. Kural 34 calls everything but a spotless mind 'noisy show', and Tirumular 1695 describes the mind itself polished by work like a great jewel.
dialectics.lens_ta: வெளி விதிகளும் ஒழுங்குகளும் மட்டும் போதாது; மன மாசின்மையும் (குறள் 34) உழைப்பால் மெருகேறிய தூய சிந்தையுமே (திருமந்திரம் 1695) மெய்யான அறம்.

dialectics.note: The Naladiyar calls the body a pot seeping filth from nine openings, dressed in skin that fools the eye; Tirumular makes the same flesh body (ஊனுடம்பு) the Lord's shrine and the mouth its gate. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar is read as judging the body's worth itself, not only rebuking lust.
dialectics.lens_en: A genuine classical clash that directly mirrors today's debate on embodiment vs. mind-uploading: is biological flesh a flawed container to escape, or a living temple where consciousness refines itself?
dialectics.lens_ta: உடலைத் தாண்டிச் செல்லலாமா அல்லது உடலிலேயே வளரலாமா என்ற இன்றைய விவாதத்தின் 1,500 ஆண்டுப் பழைய வடிவம்: உடல் வெறும் ஒழுகும் குடமா, அல்லது உயிர் வாழும் ஆலயமா?

dialectics.note: Tirumular, by Nandi's command, promises that breath tied fast keeps the body for thousands of years; 355 calls the yogi who holds the breath to make the impermanent flesh last a fool. The conflict holds if 722 is read as bodily longevity sought for its own sake and 355 as rejecting that practice, not only its misuse.
dialectics.lens_en: Speaks straight to today's radical-longevity race. On one reading, Tirumular promises that breath held fast keeps the body for thousands of years; Arunagiri calls the yogi who holds his breath to make the flesh last a fool.
dialectics.lens_ta: இன்றைய ஆயுள் நீட்டிப்புப் போட்டியோடு நேராகப் பேசும் முரண். ஒரு வாசிப்பில், மூச்சைக் கட்டினால் உடல் ஆயிரமாண்டு நிலைக்கும் என்று திருமூலர் உறுதியளிக்கிறார்; ஊன் நிலைக்கும் என்று மூச்சை அடக்கும் யோகியை ‘அசட்டு யோகி’ என்கிறார் அருணகிரியார்.

dialectics.note: Kural 269 says those with the power of austerity can leap past Death (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும்); this quatrain says no one here has leapt past Death and escaped. The conflict holds on Parimelazhagar's literal reading of 269; Kalaignar's figurative 'conquering death' softens it. Mudaliar cites 269 here.
dialectics.lens_en: Can discipline, or future biotechnology, leap past Death (கூற்றம் குதித்தல்)? Valluvar says austerity can; the Naladiyar says no one has, and draws a practical conclusion: give your wealth away now, because tomorrow the drum may sound.
dialectics.lens_ta: தவமோ எதிர்கால உயிரித் தொழில்நுட்பமோ கூற்றத்தைக் கடக்குமா? தவ ஆற்றலால் முடியும் என்கிறார் வள்ளுவர்; யாரும் கடந்ததில்லை என்கிறது நாலடியார், ஒரு நடைமுறை முடிவோடு: உங்கள் செல்வத்தை இப்போதே வழங்குங்கள், நாளை பறை ஒலிக்கலாம்.

dialectics.note: The Thiruppugazh song, its singer unlearned in Vedas and Agamas, asks for the teaching of knowledge beyond the six sixes (ஆறாறு மீதில் ஞானோபதேசம்). The Tirumanthiram verse reports that to one who did not know the nature of the six sixes (ஆறாறின் தன்மை அறியாது இருந்தேனுக்கு) Nandi made it known and stood beyond them. The same term, ஆறாறு, gives the request in one and its fulfilment through the guru in the other.
dialectics.lens_en: Unlearned in the Vedas and Agamas, the singer asks for knowledge beyond the thirty-six tattvas (ஆறாறு), the whole make-up of experience; Tirumular reports receiving it through his guru. A kind of knowing that accumulation alone does not reach.
dialectics.lens_ta: வேதமும் ஆகமமும் கற்காத பாடகர் ஆறாறு தத்துவங்களுக்கு அப்பாலான ஞானத்தைக் கேட்கிறார்; குருவின் அருளால் அதைப் பெற்றதைத் திருமூலர் சொல்கிறார். வெறும் சேகரிப்பால் எட்ட முடியாத அறிதல் இது.
